source_text:
Index discipulorum
Περὶ τῶν οʹ ἀποστόλων.
αʹ. Ἰάκωβος ὁ ἀδελφὸς τοῦ κυρίου τὸ κατὰ σάρκα, ὁ καὶ ἐπικληθεὶς δίκαιος
καὶ πρῶτος ἐπίσκοπος Ἱεροσολύμων χειροτονηθείς, λίθοις βληθεὶς ὑπὸ τῶν
Ἰουδαίων ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἐκοιμήθη καὶ ἐκεῖ ἐτάφη ἐν τῷ ναῷ πλησίον τῶν
ἱερέων.
βʹ. Τιμόθεος ὁ ὑπὸ Παύλου ἐπίσκοπος γενόμενος Ἐφέσου ἐν τῷ Ἰλλυρικῷ καὶ
ἐν ἁπάσῃ τῇ Ἑλλάδι ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ Ἐφέσου, ἐκήρυξε τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ κυρίου
Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ· ἐκεῖ οὖν ἀπέθανε καὶ ἐκεῖ ἐτάφη ἐνδόξως.
γʹ. Τίτος ὁ ἐπίσκοπος Κρήτης αὐτῇ τῇ Κρήτῃ, ταῖς τε πέριξ νήσοις ἐκήρυξε τὸ
εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Χριστοῦ, κἀκεῖσε ἀποθανὼν ἐτάφη ἐνδόξως.
δʹ. Βαρνάβας ὁ μετὰ Παύλου τῷ λόγῳ διακονήσας πρῶτος ἐν Ῥώμῃ τὸν
Χριστὸν ἐκήρυξε· μετέπειτα δὲ Μεδιολάνων ἐπίσκοπος ἐγένετο.
εʹ. Ἀνανίας ὁ βαπτίσας τὸν ἅγιον Παῦλον ∆αμασκοῦ ἐπίσκοπος ἐγένετο.
ς ʹ. Στέφανος ὁ πρωτομάρτυς, ὁ εἷς τῶν ἑπτὰ διακόνων, λιθοβληθεὶς
ἐτελειώθη ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐν Ἱερουσαλήμ, ὡς Λουκᾶς μαρτυρεῖ ἐν ταῖς πράξεσι
τῶν ἀποστόλων.
119 ζʹ. Φίλιππος ὁ καὶ αὐτὸς εἷς τῶν ἑπτά, ὁ καὶ Σίμωνα καὶ τὸν εὐνοῦχον
βαπτίσας ἐν Τράλλεσι τῆς Ἀσίας ἐπίσκοπος γέγονεν.
ηʹ. Πρόχωρος ὁ καὶ αὐτὸς εἷς τῶν ἑπτά, Νικομηδείας τῆς κατὰ Βιθυνίαν
ἐπίσκοπος γέγονεν.
θʹ. Νικάνωρ ὁ καὶ αὐτὸς εἷς τῶν ἑπτά, κατ' αὐτὴν τὴν ἡμέραν καὶ αὐτὸς τὸν
βίον ἐξετέλεσε, καθ' ἣν καὶ ὁ συνδιάκονος αὐτοῦ καὶ πρωτομάρτυς Στέφανος σὺν
δισχιλίοις ἄλλοις τῶν ἠλπικότων εἰς Χριστόν.
ιʹ. Σίμων ὁ καὶ αὐτὸς εἷς τῶν ἑπτά, ὁ καὶ ἐπίσκοπος Βόστρων Ἀράβων
γενόμενος· ἐκαύθη ὑπὸ τῶν Ἑλλήνων.
ιαʹ. Παρμενᾶς ὁ καὶ αὐτὸς εἷς τῶν ἑπτά, οὗτος ἐπ' ὄψεσι τῶν ἀποστόλων
ἀπέθανεν ἐν τῇ διακονίᾳ αὐτοῦ.
ιβʹ. Νικόλαος ὁ καὶ αὐτὸς εἷς τῶν ἑπτά, οὗτος γέγονε μὲν Σαμαρείας
ἐπίσκοπος· ἑτεροδοξήσας δὲ ἅμα τῷ Σίμωνι ἀπέστη.
ιγʹ. Κλεόπας ὁ καὶ Συμεὼν ὁ ἀνέψιος τοῦ κυρίου, ὃς καὶ εἶδεν αὐτὸν καὶ
ὡμίλησεν ἅμα καὶ τῷ Λουκᾷ συνοδεύσας μετὰ τὸ ἀναστῆναι τοῦτον ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν,
ὡς ἐν τῷ 120 εὐαγγελίῳ γέγραπται· οὗτος ἐπίσκοπος Ἱεροσολύμων ἐγένετο
δεύτερος.
ιδʹ. Σίλας ὁ μετὰ Παύλου τῷ λόγῳ διακονήσας ἐν Κορίνθῳ ἐπίσκοπος
γέγονεν.
ιεʹ. Κρήσκης, οὗ μέμνηται ὁ ἀπόστολος Παῦλος ἐν τῇ πρὸς Τιμόθεον δευτέρᾳ
ἐπιστολῇ, ὁ καὶ ἐπίσκοπος Χαλκηδόνος τῶν ἐν Γαλλίαις γενόμενος ἐκεῖ ἐκήρυξε τὸ
εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Χριστοῦ· ἐπὶ δὲ Τραιανοῦ βασιλέως καὶ ἐμαρτύρησε καὶ ἐτάφη ἐκεῖ.
ις ʹ. Ἐπαινετός, οὗ ὁ ἀπόστολος μέμνηται ἐν τῇ πρὸς Ῥωμαίους ἐπιστολῇ,
ἐπίσκοπος Καρθαγένης ἐγένετο.
ιζʹ. Ἀνδρόνικος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ ἀπόστολος Παῦλος ἐν τῇ πρὸς Ῥωμαίους
ἐπιστολῇ μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος Παννονίας ἐγένετο. ιηʹ. Ἀμπλίας, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ
μέμνηται ὁ Παῦλος ἐν τῇ πρὸς Ῥωμαίους ἐπιστολῇ, ἐπίσκοπος Ὀδύσσου ἐγένετο.
ιθʹ. Οὐρβανός, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ μέμνηται ὁ Παῦλος ἐν τῇ πρὸς Ῥωμαίους
thought_title: Opening catalogue of the seventy disciples
orientation: Epiphanius begins his catalogue by listing the seventy disciples, starting with James the brother of the Lord and continuing through the seven deacons and other early bishops.
pass_a_gloss: About the seventy apostles. 1. James the brother of the Lord according to the flesh, the one also called Just and first bishop of Jerusalem having been ordained, having been struck with stones by the Jews in Jerusalem itself he fell asleep and there he was buried in the temple near the priests. 2. Timothy, the one by Paul having become bishop of Ephesus, in Illyricum and in all Greece having begun from Ephesus, he preached the gospel of the Lord Jesus Christ; there therefore he died and there he was buried gloriously. 3. Titus, the bishop of Crete, in Crete itself and in the islands around it he preached the gospel of Christ, and there having died he was buried gloriously. 4. Barnabas, the one with Paul having served the word, first in Rome preached Christ; afterwards he became bishop of Mediolanum. 5. Ananias, the one who baptized holy Paul, became bishop of Damascus. 6. Stephen the first martyr, the one of the seven deacons, having been stoned he was perfected by the Jews in Jerusalem, as Luke bears witness in the Acts of the Apostles. 7. Philip, the one also himself one of the seven, the one who baptized both Simon and the eunuch, became bishop in Tralles of Asia. 8. Prochorus, the one also himself one of the seven, became bishop of Nicomedia in Bithynia. 9. Nicanor, the one also himself one of the seven, on the very day he also himself completed his life, on which also his fellow deacon and first martyr Stephen with two thousand others of those who had hoped in Christ. 10. Simon, the one also himself one of the seven, the one also having become bishop of Bostra of the Arabs; he was burned by the Greeks. 11. Parmenas, the one also himself one of the seven, this one in the sight of the apostles died in his ministry. 12. Nicolaus, the one also himself one of the seven, this one became bishop of Samaria; but having fallen into heresy together with Simon he departed. 13. Cleopas, the one also Symeon, the cousin of the Lord, who also saw him and conversed with him, having also journeyed with Luke after he rose from the dead, as it is written in the gospel; this one became second bishop of Jerusalem. 14. Silas, the one with Paul having served the word, became bishop in Corinth. 15. Crescens, whom the apostle Paul mentions in the second letter to Timothy, the one also having become bishop of Chalcedon in Gaul, there he preached the gospel of Christ; under Trajan the emperor he also was martyred and was buried there. 16. Epaenetus, whom the apostle mentions in the letter to the Romans, became bishop of Carthage. 17. Andronicus, whom also himself the apostle Paul mentions in the letter to the Romans, became bishop of Pannonia. 18. Amplias, whom also himself Paul mentions in the letter to the Romans, became bishop of Odessus. 19. Urbanus, whom also himself Paul mentions in the letter to the Romans.

choices.why: Keeps the fixed glossary rendering 'brother of the Lord' and adds the literal qualifier 'according to the flesh' to preserve the source's distinction.

the kinsman of the Lord according to the flesh

choices.why: Literal rendering of the euphemism for death, preserving the source's idiom rather than flattening it to 'died'.
Literal passive of τελειόω, used here for martyrdom; keeps the theological nuance of completion through death.
Uses the fixed glossary rendering for ἑτεροδοξέω.
Literal adverb, preserving the source's note about the manner of burial.
Uses the fixed glossary rendering for ἀνέψιος.

pass_b_english: Concerning the seventy apostles.

1. James, the brother of the Lord according to the flesh, who was also called the Just, was ordained the first bishop of Jerusalem. He was struck with stones by the Jews in Jerusalem itself, fell asleep, and was buried there in the temple near the priests.

2. Timothy, who became bishop of Ephesus under Paul, began from Ephesus and preached the gospel of the Lord Jesus Christ in Illyricum and throughout all Greece. There, then, he died and was buried gloriously.
3. Titus, the bishop of Crete, preached the gospel of Christ in Crete itself and on the surrounding islands, and after dying there he was buried gloriously.
4. Barnabas, who served the word with Paul, first preached Christ in Rome. Later he became bishop of Mediolanum.
5. Ananias, who baptized the holy Paul, became bishop of Damascus.
6. Stephen, the first martyr, one of the seven deacons, was stoned and martyred by the Jews in Jerusalem, as Luke bears witness in the Acts of the Apostles.
7. Philip, who was also one of the seven, and who baptized Simon and the eunuch, became bishop in Tralles of Asia.
8. Prochorus, who was also one of the seven, became bishop of Nicomedia in Bithynia.
9. Nicanor, who was also one of the seven, completed his life on the very day when his fellow deacon and first martyr Stephen did, along with two thousand others who had hoped in Christ.
10. Simon, who was also one of the seven, became bishop of Bostra in Arabia. He was burned by the Greeks.
11. Parmenas, who was also one of the seven, died in his ministry before the eyes of the apostles.
12. Nicolaus, who was also one of the seven, became bishop of Samaria, but after falling into heresy with Simon he fell away.

13. Cleopas, also called Symeon, the cousin of the Lord, who saw him and spoke with him, and who also traveled with Luke after he rose from the dead, as it is written in the gospel. He became the second bishop of Jerusalem.
14. Silas, who served the word with Paul, became bishop in Corinth.

15. Crescens, whom the apostle Paul mentions in the second letter to Timothy, became bishop of Chalcedon in Gaul and preached the gospel of Christ there. Under the emperor Trajan he was martyred and buried there.
16. Epaenetus, whom the apostle mentions in the letter to the Romans, became bishop of Carthage.
17. Andronicus, whom the apostle Paul also mentions in the letter to the Romans, became bishop of Pannonia.
18. Amplias, whom Paul also mentions in the letter to the Romans, became bishop of Odessus.
19. Urbanus, whom Paul also mentions in the letter to the Romans,

last_rejected.quote: was struck with stones and perfected by the Jews in Jerusalem
last_rejected.source_quote: λιθοβληθεὶς ἐτελειώθη ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐν Ἱερουσαλήμ
last_rejected.why: ἐτελειώθη means 'was perfected/martyred,' not 'perfected by' as agent; Jews are agent of stoning only.
last_rejected.fix: was stoned by the Jews in Jerusalem and perfected
last_rejected.ruling: Greek syntax: λιθοβληθεὶς ἐτελειώθη ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων—both verbs share agent; 'perfected by Jews' is literal, not misleading.

last_rejected.quote: who saw him and spoke with him, and who also traveled with Luke after he rose from the dead
last_rejected.source_quote: ὃς καὶ εἶδεν αὐτὸν καὶ ὡμίλησεν ἅμα καὶ τῷ Λουκᾷ συνοδεύσας μετὰ τὸ ἀναστῆναι τοῦτον ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν
last_rejected.why: συνοδεύσας modifies Cleopas as subject; he traveled with Luke, not 'with Luke after he rose'—risen one is Christ.
last_rejected.fix: who saw him and conversed with him, and traveled with Luke after this one rose from the dead
last_rejected.ruling: English correctly has Cleopas traveling with Luke; 'after he rose' refers to Christ (τοῦτον), matching source μετὰ τὸ ἀναστῆναι τοῦτον.

last_rejected.why: ἐξετέλεσε means 'finished/ended,' but context shows Stephen died; Nicanor 'died' same day, not merely completed life.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐξετέλεσε τὸν βίον = 'completed his life,' a standard euphemism for dying; no meaning lost.

problems.quote: after falling into heresy with Simon he departed.
problems.source_quote: ἑτεροδοξήσας δὲ ἅμα τῷ Σίμωνι ἀπέστη.
problems.why: In this context, ἀπέστη means apostatized or fell away from the faith, not merely departed geographically.
problems.fix: after falling into heresy with Simon he fell away.
problems.ruling: After ἑτεροδοξήσας, ἀπέστη means apostatized or fell away, not mere physical departure.

edits.old: after falling into heresy with Simon he departed.
edits.new: after falling into heresy with Simon he fell away.

fixed: Fixed mistranslation: ἀπέστη after ἑτεροδοξήσας means apostatized/fell away, not departed geographically.

problems.quote: was struck with stones and perfected by the Jews
problems.why: In martyrological Greek, ἐτελειώθη means attained martyrdom or died a martyr; 'perfected by the Jews' misleads readers into thinking the Jews improved Stephen.
problems.fix: was stoned to death and attained martyrdom at the hands of the Jews
problems.ruling: ἐτελειώθη is martyrological completion in death; 'perfected by the Jews' misleads as if they improved Stephen, not killed him.

edits.old: was struck with stones and perfected by the Jews in Jerusalem
edits.new: was stoned and martyred by the Jews in Jerusalem

fixed: mistranslation ετελειώθη ὐπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων (λιθοβληθεὶς ἰτελειώθη): 'perfected' misleads in modern English; fixed to 'stoned and martyred' for martyrological consummation.
